title: Atlas provider SDK CLI security assessment
scope: Official SDK provider scaffolding, trusted local factory loading, manifest inspection, local conformance, and evidence export

approved_targets: Disposable generated provider projects under test and smoke directories
prohibited_actions: Overwrite an existing project or evidence file
Represent scaffold conformance as vendor certification

actors: Explicitly selected trusted local provider factory
trust_boundaries: CLI arguments to filesystem scaffold generation
Manifest JSON to strict ProviderManifest validation
Developer-selected module factory to local Python execution
Certification receipt to exclusive evidence file
data_flows: Validated scaffold arguments into a new atomic project directory
Bounded UTF-8 JSON manifest into safe capability metadata
Trusted local factory into static assessment or explicitly selected dynamic local-sandbox conformance
Payload-free receipt into stdout and optional new JSON evidence file

threats.name: Scaffold overwrites developer work
threats.control: The target must not exist; generation occurs in an owned sibling staging directory and is renamed only after every file is complete.

threats.name: Manifest smuggles secrets or unsafe configuration
threats.control: Input is bounded to 64 KiB, unknown fields are rejected, booleans are strict, and ProviderManifest rejects URLs, offline credentials, and invalid environments.

threats.name: Factory reference creates unexpected code execution
threats.control: The command explicitly states trusted local factory semantics, accepts only package.module:function syntax, uses importlib without eval or shell execution, and is never exposed through Gateway or Operator.

threats.name: Dynamic certification invokes a live provider
threats.control: Dynamic mode must be explicitly requested and ProviderCertificationRunner executes only offline, credential-free, synthetic local-sandbox manifests.

threats.name: Evidence overwrites or leaks sensitive data
threats.control: Evidence uses exclusive creation, a required JSON suffix, safe receipt fields, bounded check details, and no endpoint hosts, payloads, credential values, or raw exception text.

findings.finding: The generated starter passes the same provider conformance contract as the built-in Hotel PMS sandbox.
Importing a selected Python factory executes that local module. Developers must review and trust the code before using certify.
Generated local conformance is not vendor certification or production authorization.

validation: The full Atlas suite passed 104 of 104 tests, including five focused provider CLI cases.
Generated project completed dynamic local-sandbox certification.
Existing project and evidence overwrite attempts were rejected without changing retained files.
Generated and source Python compiled successfully.
residual_risk: Trusted local factory loading is intentional Python code execution and cannot sandbox malicious developer code.
No dependency lock, signature, or independent vendor attestation is generated by this CLI.
A networked adapter requires separate authorization, secrets design, endpoint controls, and focused security review.
Recheck this assessment before adding plugin discovery, remote invocation, or production promotion.
